You can help FinKore by making a financial rule easier to understand or review. Useful contributions include:

  • Clarifying documentation, fixing a link, or improving a reading path.
  • Reviewing a requirement for ambiguity or inconsistency with CoreDoc.
  • Reporting an undefined result with explicit inputs and its financial impact.
  • Adding portable acceptance cases for existing requirements, including failure, boundary, and mutation-sensitive cases.
  • Improving the domain-neutral tools that validate repository artifacts.

FinKore is specification-first. Consumer financial implementations and execution tools belong in consumer repositories.

Make your first contribution

  1. Choose one concrete problem. A confusing paragraph or broken link can be a small first change; explain what the reader needs to understand.
  2. Read the relevant sources using the repository map below. For financial behavior, read CoreDoc, the owning specification, related manifest-listed vectors and traceability, then applicable Agentic metadata.
  3. Use Issues on the GitHub project for ordinary defects and concrete proposals, and Discussions for questions or early ideas. Discuss behavior changes before selecting new semantics. A small editorial fix can go directly to a Pull Request. Potentially exploitable findings follow the Security Policy privately.
  4. Fork the repository, clone your fork, and create a focused branch, for example with git switch -c docs/clarify-reading-path.
  5. Make the change in its canonical source. For a Markdown source that feeds Learn, regenerate the HTML and include both source and output in the same PR.
  6. Run the checks below and review the diff, including generated content. For Learn changes, review desktop and mobile reading, keyboard navigation, section links, tables, code, and horizontal overflow.
  7. Push your branch to your fork and open a Pull Request into main. Explain the problem, resulting behavior or wording, affected requirements when applicable, and validation performed. Link any related Issue and respond to review comments.

Find the source

DirectoryResponsibility
docs/coreDoc/Foundation-level financial obligations and their governance metadata.
spec/Precise normative behavior, stable requirement IDs, invariants, and portable errors.
conformance/Manifest, schemas, portable acceptance cases, consumer guidance, and traceability.
agentic/Canonical operation semantics and safety metadata for machine clients.
docs/tools/Domain-neutral maintenance tools, their tests, and verification guidance.
learn/The public introduction, generated document readers, and local presentation assets.

Edit canonical Markdown before regenerating its Learn reader. The source-to-reader table lists the mappings. learn/index.html has its own editorial content and a marked CoreDoc index generated from docs/coreDoc/core-doc.md; update that block through its source or renderer. Other generated readers are updated through their Markdown sources or renderers, not by editing the output HTML.

Set up and verify

The maintenance tools require Node >=24.11.0 <25. Check your runtime first:

node --version
npm --version

If the runtime is missing or outside that range, follow the supported Node setup, including the repository-local .tools option, before running npm commands.

For a source that feeds Learn, run this workflow from the repository root:

npm ci --no-audit
npm run learn:build
git diff --check
git diff
npm run verify

Review the generated diff before submitting it with the source. For changes that do not affect Learn sources or renderers, omit npm run learn:build. See editing Learn pages for details.

The same npm run verify command runs locally and in GitHub Actions. It checks published artifacts and maintenance tools; it does not execute financial operations against a consumer implementation. Run npm run dependencies:audit as a separate network-backed dependency review when the release or maintenance task requires one.

Editorial fixes and behavior proposals

An editorial correction improves wording or navigation while preserving every observable result, stable identifier, and CoreDoc evolution field. Follow SPEC-COMPATIBILITY-011 and synchronize any affected Learn readers.

A behavior proposal begins with the domain problem and CoreDoc alignment. State the inputs, current requirement, expected observation, and financial or control impact. If the result is undefined, report the gap rather than choosing semantics from a fixture or a language default. Follow the coordinated review below before changing portable expectations.

Open contributions and maintainer authority

Anyone may fork FinKore, open Issues, participate in Discussions, propose modifications, review and challenge specifications, and submit Pull Requests. Lead maintainer @willgittens retains final integration authority.

CODEOWNERS assigns repository-wide review ownership to @willgittens. It documents responsibility and requests reviews; it does not grant or restrict merge permissions. Potentially exploitable technical or financial specification defects must follow the Security Policy for private reporting rather than public Issues or Discussions.

Compatibility and coordinated review

An accepted normative correction must update its owning specification, conformance vectors or traceability, applicable Agentic metadata, public documentation, and any affected repository-maintenance tests in the same change. When observable behavior changes, document the compatibility and consumer migration impact. Consumer-owned implementation changes and execution evidence belong in consumer repositories and are not a same-commit prerequisite for this repository.

Use the specification compatibility policy to classify changes and preserve published identifiers, portable errors, operation contracts, and serializations. Retired requirement identifiers remain unavailable for reuse; consult Git history and the release notes before assigning an identifier.

For a retirement, review the exact requirement diff, remove obsolete active references and traceability rows, and recompute inventory totals. Preserve all continuing obligations and keep original definitions in Git history. Record the sunset and compatibility impact concisely under Unreleased in the existing release notes, then include that note in the release entry when released.

Editorial changes follow SPEC-COMPATIBILITY-011. A changed observable result needs specification-first review and coordinated artifact updates as described above, even when discovered while adding a regression case.

For the stable Core contract, patch releases contain compatible clarifications, tooling fixes, documentation corrections, and defects that do not redefine the contract. Minor releases add backward-compatible behavior or independent domains. Incompatible changes to existing requirements, errors, operations, or serializations require a new major Core release. Manifest and vector syntax versions remain separate from Core versions.

New financial behavior follows specification-first review, portable acceptance cases, traceability, and Agentic metadata where applicable. Review positive, negative, boundary, failure-atomicity, and mutation-sensitive cases alongside local artifact verification. Ledger posting, Payments, Tax, Reconciliation, and other deferred domains need an explicitly accepted scope before development; they do not enter stable maintenance work implicitly.

Licensing of Contributions

FinKore community source code is licensed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPL-2.0). By submitting a contribution to an MPL-2.0-covered portion of FinKore, you agree that the contribution is submitted under the licensing terms applicable to that portion of the repository, unless explicitly agreed otherwise in writing.

Do not remove or alter required license notices, third-party notices, or SPDX identifiers. If your contribution includes or derives from third-party material, disclose that provenance clearly in the pull request or issue.

This project does not currently require a Contributor License Agreement or copyright assignment. Future contributor-rights governance remains an open decision; see Contributor Licensing.

Nothing in this document is legal advice.

Maintainer responsibilities

The remaining sections cover repository administration and stable publication. They are maintained by the lead maintainer; contributors can submit a PR using the workflow above without configuring upstream access or preparing a release.

Manual GitHub configuration

The maintainer must configure these settings in GitHub; repository files do not activate Rulesets or change access permissions:

  1. Under Settings → Collaborators and any applicable organization access settings, verify that only @willgittens has administrative or merge authority. Review direct access, inherited roles, installed Apps, deploy keys, and automation that can write to main. Community participation does not require upstream write access.
  2. Under Settings → Rules → Rulesets, create or activate a branch Ruleset targeting main. Require a Pull Request and the exact status check Verify repository from GitHub Actions after its first successful run. Block force pushes and branch deletion. Keep the approval count at zero and code-owner approval disabled so the sole maintainer can merge their own Pull Requests. Give this verification Ruleset no bypass actors.
  3. If additional upstream writers are introduced, use a separate main Ruleset with Restrict updates, allowing only the lead maintainer's role to bypass it for Pull Requests only. Verify that the bypass role contains only @willgittens. Keep this restriction separate from the verification Ruleset so it does not bypass CI. Reassess access if that role gains members.
  4. Under Settings → Actions → General, permit the workflow and its two official actions, retain a read-only workflow token, and keep write tokens and secrets unavailable to fork PR workflows. Review fork-workflow approval settings.
  5. Under Settings → Advanced Security, confirm Private Vulnerability Reporting is enabled and the repository's Security → Advisories page offers Report a vulnerability. If unavailable, follow the fallback in the Security Policy before considering private reporting operational.
  6. Once these files are on main, check that GitHub recognizes .github/CODEOWNERS without errors and shows @willgittens as owner for a specification file and the workflow. Review requests use the base branch's CODEOWNERS; authors do not receive requests to review their own PRs.

Working plans and published guidance

Working plans are temporary development material. Preserve their reviewed state in ordinary Git history before removing completed or superseded plans. Do not copy them to an archive or release attachment. Only an active execution plan may remain during development; remove it before stable publication once enduring procedures are in existing contributor and tool guidance. Published artifacts and verification must not require plans. Keep concise release summaries in docs/releases/README.md; detailed development history remains in Git.

Stable publication also requires npm run release:check after normal local verification. During preparation, use npm run release:check -- /path/to/tree on a disposable proposed-release copy. After final status updates and removal of the last working plan, repeat it on the actual final tree before tagging. Passing development verification does not waive this gate or the separate release dependency audit. See publication checks for status conventions, permitted historical metadata, and Learn review. The publication checker has one explicitly selected Core target version; review and update that target with its tests for each release rather than accepting whichever version strings happen to agree across a tree.

Stable release procedure

Finish the normative, conformance, Agentic, and documentation reviews before tagging. Preserve stable identifiers and CoreDoc evolution metadata, retain explicit coverage limitations, and resolve any blocking specification gap. Review the proposed tracked file list for credentials, generated reports, local toolchains, copied development material, and obsolete implementation or package instructions. Check the Learn index's rendered layout and keyboard navigation.

After removing temporary plans, run a clean locked dependency install, npm run verify, the separate network-backed npm run dependencies:audit, and npm run release:check on the actual final tree. Record the advisory-query date and dependency scope with the concise release summary in docs/releases/README.md. Failed gates block tagging; artifact checks do not establish consumer implementation conformance.

Commit the reviewed release tree, then create an annotated core-<Core version> tag on that commit (for example, core-2.0.2). Confirm the tag targets the verified commit and that the working tree is clean. Distribute only tracked release content, excluding local checkout state. Remote tag publication is a separate maintainer action; a local tag does not imply a remote release. Core publication does not publish implementation packages or a runner.
